:::{#exm-complete-inner-product-space}
#### Polynomials are not complete

Let $V$ be the real vector space of polynomials on $[0, 1]$ with the inner product $\iprod{f}{g} = \int_0^1 f(t)\,g(t)\,dt$.
The partial sums $p_n(t) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{t^k}{k!}$ are a Cauchy sequence in $V$,
because they converge uniformly on $[0, 1]$ to $e^t$.
The only candidate for a limit is $e^t$, which is not a polynomial,
so no polynomial $\vy \in V$ satisfies the condition of @def-complete-inner-product-space,
and $V$ is not complete.
<!-- no-figure: the example is a convergence argument about one sequence -->

:::
